taxonomyNote: NatureServe lists this as the Beringian ermine after the 2021 split (Colella et al.); mainland North American animals are M. richardsonii.
fieldMarks: Typical weasel form: long body, short legs, triangular head, slightly protruding round ears
White winter coat with a black tail tip
Summer: chocolate-brown back, yellowish-white underside up to the upper lip
Body 170-330 mm; tail about 35% of body length; males about twice the mass of females
behavior: Uses riparian woodlands, marshes, fencerows and open areas next to forest
Climbs trees and swims well; dens in tree roots, hollow logs, stone walls and rodent burrows
habitat: Riparian woodlands, marshes, shrubby fencerows and open areas adjacent to forest or shrub borders.
range: Much of Eurasia; in North America, Alaska and western Yukon to most of Arctic Canada and east to Greenland per NatureServe. The widespread North American animal is now M. richardsonii.

lookalikes.name: American ermine
lookalikes.howToTell: Same appearance; separated by range, with M. richardsonii across most of Canada and the northern US.
